card: Reject unrecognized options passed to the sendall RPC method rather than silently ignoring them, and remove the unused solving_data option. Callers currently face unintended wallet behavior when making typos in option names, such as spending all wallet UTXOs instead of an intended subset if inputs is misspelled, or accidentally broadcasting a transaction if psbt or add_to_wallet is misspelled. Existing RPCs like send and fundrawtransaction already reject unknown options.
evidence: PR description points out that a misspelled input instead of inputs spends all available UTXOs rather than the given ones, and a misspelled add_to_wallet or psbt can broadcast a transaction the caller asked not to broadcast.
PR description notes that send, fundrawtransaction, walletcreatefundedpsbt, and bumpfee already reject unknown options.
problem: When calling sendall, unknown or misspelled option keys are silently ignored. A caller who typos an option like inputs as input will unintentionally spend all available UTXOs instead of the specified subset, and a misspelled add_to_wallet or psbt option can cause an unintended transaction broadcast.

risk.why: Strict option validation will cause RPC calls with unexpected or typoed fields to fail with an error, potentially breaking poorly written scripts while preventing silent misbehavior.

summary: Rejects unrecognized keys in the options dictionary of the sendall RPC method instead of silently ignoring them. It also removes the unused solving_data option from sendall and documents the behavior change in a release note.
